props.gloss_en: the first tanna: the hole in the ear [that is a blemish] is the size of a karshina
R' Yosei b'R' Yehuda: the hole is the size of a lentil
a tanna taught: their words are close to being equal
(entertained) the 'close' words are those of the first tanna and R' Yosei ben HaMeshullam
(inside the hypothesis) there is much between them
rather, the words of the first tanna and R' Yosei b'R' Yehuda [karshina and lentil]
R' Yosei b'R' Yehuda: 'and you shall take' (Deut 15:17) -- anything taken by hand, including a thorn, a needle, a gimlet and a stylus, is valid for piercing the slave's ear
Rabbi: 'awl' -- as an awl is distinct in being of metal, so anything of metal
Yudan beRabbi expounded: when they pierce, they pierce only in the earlobe
the Chachamim: a Hebrew slave who is a kohen is not pierced, because he becomes blemished
the Chachamim: if they pierced in the earlobe, how would a kohen slave become blemished? so they pierce only at the top of the ear
Rav Chana bar Ketina: here [the lentil] is for slaughtering [the firstborn on its account]; there [any hole] is for disqualifying
Rav Sherevya: karshina is hinda (bitter vetch)
(queried) the measure is a karshina that enters and leaves the hole
(queried) the measure is a karshina that stands [fixed] in the hole
Rav Huna Rabba: this I did not hear; its like I heard (and he brings the Oholot drill-hole case, 37b.17-38a.2)
Beit Shammai: a spine lacking two vertebrae does not impart tent-impurity
Beit Hillel: lacking one vertebra
Beit Shammai: a skull lacking the size of a drill-hole
Beit Hillel: lacking enough that, removed from a living man, he would die
Shmuel: [Beit Hillel's] 'enough that, removed from a living man, he dies' is the size of a sela
Rav Safra: [Rav Tachlifa] told him an amoraic tradition
Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda: he told him a tannaitic teaching
the mishna: a window not made by man -- its measure is a large fist, the fist of Ben Avatiach
R' Yosei: and it is as a large human head
the mishna: a man-made window -- they measured it as the large drill of the chamber
the mishna: which is as the Italian pundeyon, and as a Neronian sela, and as the hole of a yoke
Beit Shammai's 'drill-hole' is the drill with its blockage (a hole the drill enters and leaves) -- somewhat larger than a sela
Rav Huna Rabba's analogy: the karshina-measure is like Beit Shammai's drill-measure, which is a hole the drill enters and leaves
Rabban Gamliel HaZaken (via Chizkiya avi Ikkesh): whatever among earthenware has no receptacle has no division of back [from inside]: inside impure -- back impure, back impure -- inside impure
R' Yitzchak bar Avin: thus it says -- whatever has no receptacle among earthenware [is pure]; its counterpart among rinsable vessels has no division of back
it teaches that a rinsable vessel WITH a receptacle is like earthenware: inside impure -- back impure; inside not impure -- back not impure
for Torah impurity, indeed so; here it speaks of the rabbinic impurity of liquids
the mishna: a vessel whose back was defiled by liquids -- its back is impure; its inside, rim, ear and handles pure; inside impure -- all of it impure
by Torah law neither food nor liquid defiles a vessel; the Rabbis decreed it on account of the liquids of a zav and zava
so the Rabbis made it like earthenware impurity, not like its own Torah impurity
the Rabbis made a marker, so that teruma and kodashim not be burnt on its account
since they made a marker for the vessel with a receptacle, it is known that [the liquid-impurity of] one without a receptacle is rabbinic
[the receptacle-less rinsable vessels meant are] those fit for midras
there is no midras impurity in earthenware
Rav Pappa: [the drill equal to the sela, in the window mishna] is the LARGE drill that we learned
by inference, a plain drill [Beit Shammai's] is smaller than a sela
R' Meir: [Beit Shammai's drill] is the small drill of physicians
the Chachamim: it is the large drill of the chamber
the leniencies of Beit Shammai and stringencies of Beit Hillel that we learned, we learned; those we did not learn, we did not learn
Rav Nachman: it is the NERONIAN sela that we learned to equal the large drill
Rav Nachman: a plain sela [Shmuel's, for Beit Hillel] is smaller than a plain drill [Beit Shammai's]

Rav Chisda: 'enough that removed from a living man [he dies]' -- how much? -- Rav Tachlifa bar Avudimi in Shmuel's name: as a sela
